title: School guidance support and growth in mathematics discourse feedback skills: a three-wave longitudinal mediation study
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether school guidance support is associated with students’ growth in mathematics discourse feedback skills, and whether that relationship operates through two mechanisms: major decision-making self-efficacy and feedback literacy behavior. The authors frame mathematics discourse feedback skills as the ability to interpret feedback, justify reasoning, monitor progress, diagnose errors, and revise work during classroom dialogue.

The study uses a three-wave longitudinal survey design with Chinese senior high school students. School guidance support was measured at Time 1, major decision-making self-efficacy at Time 2, feedback literacy behavior at Time 3, and mathematics discourse feedback skills at all three waves. The sample included 2,120 adolescents from three high schools in Hebei, China, and the analyses used structural equation modeling with autoregressive controls, demographic covariates, and bootstrapped indirect effects.

Results showed that higher perceived school guidance support predicted later mathematics discourse feedback skills both directly and indirectly. The indirect effects operated through major decision-making self-efficacy and through feedback literacy behavior, and a sequential pathway from guidance support to self-efficacy to feedback literacy behavior to math discourse feedback skills was also supported. The authors conclude that school-level guidance can foster discipline-specific feedback skills by strengthening students’ confidence in making academic decisions and by encouraging habitual feedback-seeking and feedback-use behaviors.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed three-wave longitudinal correlational study with structural equation modeling and measurement invariance testing, but it is not an experimental design and cannot support strong causal inference. It provides moderate methodological rigor for an observational design, so the evidence quality is yellow.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports statistically significant but correlational effects in a general high-school sample, with the main outcome being a proximal skill construct rather than a direct achievement gain. The effects are meaningful but not clearly intervention-tested, so the impact tier is yellow.

finding.finding_summary: This three-wave longitudinal study found that school guidance support was positively associated with later mathematics discourse feedback skills among Chinese senior high school students. In the sequential mediation model, the direct effect remained significant (β=0.112, p=0.001), and the total effect was β=0.371; the model included n=1,938 at T3 and controlled for prior math discourse feedback skills and demographics.
finding.measure: Mathematics discourse feedback skills (MDFSS) across T1-T3
finding.effect_size: β=0.371 total effect; β=0.112 direct effect

finding.finding_summary: School guidance support positively predicted major decision-making self-efficacy, a motivational belief reflecting confidence in gathering information, making academic choices, and persisting under uncertainty. In the sequential mediation model, guidance support predicted self-efficacy strongly (β=0.545, p<0.001), and the indirect pathway through self-efficacy was significant (β=0.070 to 0.126 depending on model).
finding.study_size: n=2,120 at T1; longitudinal subset n=1,938
finding.confidence_interval: self-efficacy path not_reported; indirect effects [0.033, 0.109] and [0.107, 0.142]
